acceptanceCriteria: The system displays the promo code discount amount for both the outbound trip and the return trip in the Mozio email confirmation when a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied.
The system calculates the promo code discount amount for the return trip independently from the outbound trip, reflecting the correct discounted fare for each leg of the return journey.
The system renders the promo code discount line item for the return trip in the same format and position as the outbound trip within the email confirmation template.
The system displays the promo code discount amount as zero or omits the discount line for the return trip when no promo code is applied to the order, without causing a template rendering error.

The system correctly displays the promo code discount for both trip legs when the outbound and return trips have different base fares, ensuring the discount is proportional or correctly allocated per the business rules.

The system handles orders with multiple line items on the return trip (e.g., multiple passengers or ticket types) by displaying the aggregated promo code discount amount for the return portion in the email confirmation.

The system logs a warning and still sends the email confirmation with the outbound discount displayed when the promo code discount calculation for the return trip fails due to missing or malformed trip metadata in the order payload.

The system displays the promo code discount amount for the return trip in the email confirmation when the order locale is set to a non-English language, using the appropriate localized currency and number formatting.

The return-trip promo code discount line item appears in the same format, position, and styling as the outbound discount line item within the email confirmation template, ensuring visual consistency across both legs.

When no promo code is applied to the order, the email confirmation either shows a zero-value discount line for the return trip or omits the line entirely, and the template renders without errors in either case.

When the outbound and return trips have different base fares, the promo code discount for each leg is allocated per business rules (e.g., proportional or per-leg rule), and the email displays the correctly allocated discount amount for each leg.

When the return trip contains multiple line items (e.g., multiple passengers or ticket types), the email confirmation displays a single aggregated promo code discount amount for the return portion that equals the sum of per-line-item discounts.

If promo code discount calculation for the return trip fails due to missing or malformed trip metadata in the order payload, the system logs a warning, still sends the email with the outbound discount displayed, and does not throw or leave the return discount line in a broken or partial state.

When the order locale is set to a non-English language, the return-trip promo code discount amount is displayed with appropriate localized currency symbols and number formatting, matching the locale formatting used for the outbound discount line.

acceptanceCriteria: When a return-trip order with a promo code is confirmed, the Mozio email confirmation renders a promo code discount line item for BOTH the outbound leg and the return leg, each showing the correct discount amount for its respective trip.

Given a return-trip order where the correct promo code discount for the return leg differs from the outbound leg's discount, the email confirmation displays distinct discount amounts for each leg — the return leg discount is not a duplicate of the outbound leg discount.

The return-trip promo code discount line item appears in the same format, position, and styling as the outbound discount line item within the email confirmation template, ensuring visual consistency across both legs.

When no promo code is applied to the order, the email confirmation either shows a zero-value discount line for the return trip or omits the line entirely, and the template renders without errors in either case.

When the outbound and return trips have different base fares, the promo code discount for each leg is allocated per business rules (e.g., proportional or per-leg rule), and the email displays the correctly allocated discount amount for each leg.

When the return trip contains multiple line items (e.g., multiple passengers or ticket types), the email confirmation displays a single aggregated promo code discount amount for the return portion that equals the sum of per-line-item discounts.

If promo code discount calculation for the return trip fails due to missing or malformed trip metadata in the order payload, the system logs a warning, still sends the email with the outbound discount displayed, and the return trip discount line is either omitted entirely or displays a safe default value (e.g., zero or 'N/A'), with no partial, corrupted, or placeholder content rendered.

When the order locale is set to a non-English language, the return-trip promo code discount amount is displayed with appropriate localized currency symbols and number formatting, matching the locale formatting used for the outbound discount line.

When a one-way trip order with a promo code is confirmed, the email confirmation still renders the promo code discount line item correctly for the single leg, confirming the return-trip fix does not regress one-way trip behavior.

When a promo code is applied to a return-trip order but results in a zero-value discount for the return leg (e.g., minimum fare threshold not met), the email confirmation renders without errors and the return trip discount line either shows zero or is omitted, consistent with the no-promo-code behavior.

When a promo code discount equals or exceeds the return trip base fare, the email confirmation displays the discount amount capped at the base fare (or per applicable business rules) and does not render a negative remaining fare for the return leg.

notes: Reviewed openspec's 8 ACs. Refined AC2 to replace the vague 'calculated independently' with an observable Given/When/Then outcome: distinct values when correct discounts differ. Refined AC7 to replace 'broken or partial state' with concrete observable alternatives (omitted or safe default, no partial/corrupted/placeholder content). Added 3 new ACs: (1) one-way trip regression guard — ensures the fix doesn't break existing one-way behavior; (2) zero-value promo code on return leg — edge case where promo applies but discount is $0; (3) full-fare or over-discount edge case — prevents negative fare display. Flagged AC4's either/or ambiguity and AC5's vague business-rules reference for human attention.
